svg.title: Ultrasonic distance instrument: wiring diagram
svg.desc: Pin-by-pin wiring. HC-SR04 #1: VCC to VBUS 5 V, Trig to GP20 (pin 26) with 10 kilohm to GND, Echo through 1 kilohm to GP21 (pin 27) with 2 kilohm from GP21 to GND, GND to GND, 100 nF across VCC and GND. HC-SR04 #2: the same with Trig GP18 (pin 24) and Echo GP19 (pin 25). The dividers bring the 5 V Echo down to about 3.3 V. Push button: one leg to GP17 (pin 22), the diagonal leg to GND. RGB LED module: R to GP12 (pin 16), G to GP13 (pin 17), B to GP14 (pin 19), minus to GND. Relay module: DC+ to VBUS 5 V (pin 40), DC- to GND, 100 nF and 10 to 47 microfarad across DC+ and DC-, IN to GP16 (pin 21) with a 4.7 kilohm pull-up to 3V3; contacts unwired. OLED SH1106: VCC to 3V3, GND to GND, SCL to GP5 (pin 7), SDA to GP4 (pin 6), each with a 4.7 kilohm pull-up to 3V3. 5 V is VBUS, pin 40, for the sensors and the relay; 3V3 is Pico pin 36, the red pin of every Gravity row; GND is any black pin.
svg.text: Pin by pin · single jumper wires · USB power only · sensors on 5 V, so each Echo goes through a divider
pin 36 · red pin of each row
Keep free: GP23, GP24, GP25, GP29
never connect 5 V to a GPIO pin
VBUS, pin 40 = the USB 5 V: both sensors and the relay, never to a GPIO
Pico 3V3(OUT), pin 36 = the red pin of every Gravity row: OLED and pull-ups (≤ 300 mA)
any black pin: all grounds are common
Wire with USB unplugged. Match each wire by the pin labels printed on the module:
the pin order on your module may differ from this drawing.
Dividers: before an Echo wire goes on, jumper the divider's top to the 5 V rail and
measure the rail and the middle point: 0.64–0.69 × the rail (about 3.3 V at 5.0 V).
Relay: COM, NO and NC stay unwired. Trigger jumper on L, if the module has one.
Power: computer USB port or a ≥ 1 A charger. The Gravity VIN input is not used.
